proof:
For each $q$ the anchored coefficient polytope is compact and has finitely many vertices. Any vector with $0<\lambda_q<1$ is a nontrivial combination of the self vector and its normalized remainder. Every nonself extreme representation therefore uses only other bases, and some positive input has greater height because its weighted average height is that of $q$. The directed graph from targets to charged inputs is acyclic.

For each transfer, the fixed compact partners give joint continuity by uniform continuity on compact sets and preserve convexity in $x$ by the supremum of convex functions. Transfers are monotone and commute with a finite maximum, since supremum commutes with maximum over a finite index set. Processing the height order finalizes each target before charging its inputs. Every final field satisfies the required inequalities. Induction in that same order proves that any array satisfying those inequalities and dominating the seeds dominates the produced array. Iterating the finite-max identity gives the path formula, including the length-zero seed.

For each base fix an interior ball $o_z+r_zB_d\subset K_z$. The fields are bounded on the finitely many compact original bodies times the unit sphere. A bound $L$ gives the inner homothet $o_z+(1-\varepsilon L/r_z)(K_z-o_z)$ because its support deficit in every direction is at least $\varepsilon L$. For small $\varepsilon$ this homothet is positive. Each defining sublevel set is convex and closed and nonnegativity gives nestedness inside $K_z$. For a nonself extreme representation at $q$ and inputs $x_j$ in the eroded fibers, put $x=\sum_j\lambda_j x_j$. They are all in the original bodies. The charged input $z$ alone gives $\lambda_z V_z(u,x_z)\ge V_q(u,x)$, hence
$$
u\cdot x+\varepsilon V_q(u,x)\le\sum_j\lambda_j[u\cdot x_j+\varepsilon V_j(u,x_j)]\le\sum_j\lambda_j h_{K_j}(u)\le h_{K_q}(u).
$$
For any nonextreme representation, use its decomposition into extreme coefficient vectors with the same input points and take the resulting convex combination in the eroded $q$-fiber. Grouping points of the lifted hull by base then proves equality of each integer fiber with the designated one. Its projection is $\operatorname{conv}P$, so there are no other integer fibers, and one positive fiber together with the base span proves the relative dimension.

To compute first losses, apply 84cd8a85417b0d7a separately on each singleton base $\{z\}$, with one ceiling $h_{K_z}(u)$ and the field $V_z(u,x)$, jointly convex in the singleton base and $x$. The cap remains its actual restriction with its original integer tilt. Thus the total first loss is $D=\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z} V_z(\nu_z,x)\,dS$, where $\nu_z$ is the a.e. outer unit normal and $dS=d\mathcal H^{d-1}$. The fixed-cap first loss $D(H)$ inserts the selector $1$ for full traces, $0$ if the fiber interior is missed, and the strict interior indicator for proper traces. The counting measure convention covers intervals. The remainders are uniform on a finite menu. In the fixed-cover situation of the statement the cover persists by nesting, and division by $M-\varepsilon D+o(\varepsilon)$ gives the stated first response on each critical row. The finitely many critical and strictly slack rows all have normalized masses below $\beta$ for small positive $\varepsilon$, giving the depth conclusion.

On $P=\{-m,\ldots,m\}$ the nonself extreme relations at $q$ are the brackets $i<q<j$ with right coefficient $(q-i)/(j-i)$, because an extreme coefficient vector with two affine constraints has support at most two. Fields are scalar multiples of $h_L$. Heights below zero have zero seeds and zero incoming demands. From $q\ge0$ to $j>q$ the transferred multiple, assuming $g_q=2^q$, is at most
$$
2^q\frac{j-i}{q-i}\le 2^q(1+j-q)\le 2^j.
$$
The adjacent midpoint transfer doubles the scalar and attains the upper bound at each next site, so induction gives the exact sequence. The fibers are $(1-\varepsilon g_q)L$ and the first losses are $g_q d|L|$. Summation gives $2^{m+1}-1$ relative to $d|L|$. The constant array gives homothetic fibers all with the same scale and hence compatible, with ratio $2m+1$.

statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty. Let positive compact convex $d$-bodies $K_z$ satisfy every anchored Minkowski inclusion on $P$. Give each base a nonnegative jointly continuous field $F_z(u,x)$ on $\mathbb S^{d-1}\times\mathbb R^d$, convex in $x$. Choose a linear height distinct on $P$. For each nonself extreme anchored probability vector $\lambda$ at $q$, choose a positive input $z$ of greater height than $q$, and define
$$
(T_eV)(u,x)=\lambda_z^{-1}\sup_{x_j\in K_j,\ j\ne z,\ \lambda_j>0} V(u,\lambda_z x+\sum_{j\ne z}\lambda_jx_j).
$$
Process targets in increasing height, with $V_z$ the maximum of $F_z$ and all incoming transfers. The resulting fields are pointwise least among arrays dominating the seeds and satisfying $V_z\ge T_eV_q$ for these chosen edges. Each field is the maximum of all composed directed seed transfers to its base. For all sufficiently small $\varepsilon\ge0$, the bodies
$$
K_z(\varepsilon)=\{x:u\cdot x+\varepsilon V_z(u,x)\le h_{K_z}(u)\text{ for every unit }u\}
$$
are positive and nested and satisfy all anchored inclusions exactly. Their lifted hull has precisely those integer fibers and full dimension relative to $\operatorname{aff}(P)\times\mathbb R^d$.

Let $M,Q$ be the old total mixed mass and maximum raw depth. Let $D,D(H)$ be the first total and fixed-cap losses on this path. If a finite list of fixed ambient closed halfspaces covers the old mixed set, has every mass at most $Q$, and satisfies $D(H)-(Q/M)D>0$ for every row of mass $Q$, the new maximum normalized depth is strictly below $Q/M$ for all sufficiently small positive $\varepsilon$. The critical normalized row expansion is $Q/M-\varepsilon[D(H)-(Q/M)D]/M+o(\varepsilon)$.

For $P=\{-m,\ldots,m\}$, $m\ge1$, identical centered fibers $L$, sole seed $h_L$ at $0$, and increasing height with each bracket charged to its right input, the final fields are $g_qh_L$ where $g_q=0$ for $q<0$ and $g_q=2^q$ for $q\ge0$. Total first loss divided by prescribed source loss is $2^{m+1}-1$. The constant continuation $h_L$ is also compatible and costs only $2m+1$ times the prescribed source loss.
